name: How close to the property line can you build an addition in Glendale or Pasadena?

mainEntity.name: How close to the property line can you build an addition in Glendale or Pasadena?
mainEntity.text: How close to the property line can you build an addition in Glendale or Pasadena?

acceptedAnswer.text: Setback rules determine how close an addition can come to the property line, and those rules vary by city, zoning district, and lot type. In Glendale and Pasadena, side and rear setbacks often shape the entire addition design, especially on smaller lots. Fire separation, window placement, and easements can also limit how close new walls can be to neighboring properties. Homeowners should not assume that available yard space is automatically buildable. A survey and zoning review are usually needed before final plans are drawn. If setbacks are tight, the design may need to shift toward a smaller footprint, a second-story addition, or a different room layout. Early verification avoids expensive redesign and helps determine whether the project is feasible before permit documents are prepared.
acceptedAnswer.description: The distance depends on local setback rules, zoning, and any easements or fire separation requirements. In many cases, you cannot build right to the property line, and side or rear setbacks may control the size and shape of the addition.
